publish.title: The stone that unlocked Egypt: the Rosetta Stone in 45 seconds
publish.description: How a decree in three scripts let scholars read hieroglyphs again.

scenes.headline: The stone that unlocked Egypt
scenes.narration: For centuries nobody could read Egyptian hieroglyphs. Then a broken slab of dark stone changed everything.

scenes.headline: Three dates
scenes.narration: A decree was carved in 196 BCE. French soldiers found the stone in 1799. And in 1822 Champollion announced how hieroglyphs worked.
items: 196 BCE: a decree is carved in three scripts
1799: French soldiers find it near Rosetta

scenes.headline: Three scripts, one message
scenes.narration: The same decree is written in Egyptian hieroglyphs, in Demotic, and in ancient Greek. Scholars could read Greek, so Greek became the key.

scenes.headline: A race to decipher
scenes.narration: Thomas Young made early progress. In 1822 Jean-François Champollion showed how the signs worked, and the language of Egypt could be read again.

scenes.headline: Now in London
scenes.narration: The Rosetta Stone has been on public display at the British Museum since 1802, and it is the most visited object there.

scenes.headline: Look closely
scenes.narration: If you visit, look for the three bands of writing, one above the other.
